description:
We are a team from Sri Lanka competing in the NASA Space Apps Challenge in 2026. We are interested in space, science, technology, coding, and problem-solving and like to work as a team in order to create useful and interesting projects.

We are excited to learn from each other and explore NASA's challenges
summary: Left Behind lets Ingenuity, the little Mars helicopter that was only meant to fly five times, tell its own story. It is an interactive, narrated website for students aged 10–15, built around a 3D model of the real helicopter. Students meet Ingenuity’s parts, then follow its journey in six chapters: arriving on Mars attached to Perseverance, the first flight, 72 flights explored in a data explorer built from NASA’s flight log, the final flight and what went wrong, and the legacy it left for future Mars helicopters. We chose Ingenuity because it is a machine that was left behind on Mars after it achieved far more than anyone expected. Telling the story in its own voice turns mission data into something students feel as well as learn. Real NASA photos, video, 3D models and flight data are credited on every screen, and the design stays simple so the science stays the focus. It works in a browser with no sign-up, so it can be used in classrooms, libraries and outreach events.
details:
What it does: Left Behind is an interactive storytelling website in which Ingenuity narrates its own mission. It starts on a 3D globe of Mars with a marker at Jezero Crater. Students enter a six-part story:
(1) meet Ingenuity and its parts on an explorable 3D model,
(2) arrival on Mars,
(3) the first flight,
(4) a flight explorer built from all 72 flights in NASA’s flight log,
(5) the final flight and NASA’s reconstruction of the hard landing,
(6) the legacy, including NASA’s planned SkyFall helicopters.

Why it matters: Ingenuity proved that powered flight is possible on another planet. Its story is full of engineering ideas students can understand, like thin air, spinning blades and teamwork between a rover and a helicopter. We tell it as a narrated story with real data, so students learn by exploring.

Design choices: We kept it minimal, with a clean text panel beside the visuals, so the NASA images, video and 3D model stay the focus. The story has narration with a sound on/off button. Every NASA image and video has a credit and source link on screen.

Tools: HTML, CSS and JavaScript (no build step), Three.js for 3D, GLTF and Draco-compressed models, JSON for the flight data, and GitHub Pages for hosting. It works on desktop and mobile.

Use of Artificial Intelligence:
Claude Free tier account: Making and debugging code and visuals.
Chatgpt Free tier account: Brainstorming
